copy.blurb:
A +13.6pp gap on the Qatar side. Bosnia and Herzegovina v Qatar in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Qatar stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

On Elo, Bosnia and Herzegovina comes in 20 points ahead — Bosnia and Herzegovina at 1660, Qatar at 1640. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 38%, the draw at 29%, and Qatar to win at 34%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Qatar on the win side reads 34%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 57%, the draw at 25%, and Qatar to win at 20%. Polymarket has Qatar at 20%, which prices out at American odds of +400; the model has the same side at 34%. The +13.6pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Qatar the lower bound is 29%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +8.7pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Qatar side.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 33 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.6pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +13.6pp gap across model and market on the Qatar side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Qatar at 34%; Polymarket sits at 20%.
copy.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina v Qatar · the model leans Qatar
